variants.text: Brewed the old way from a bitter highland root soured all winter in a buried jar, and taken alone from cold iron before dawn.
A rough black root-brew made unchanged for generations, swallowed in silence from a chipped tin cup in the cold hour.
The old highland way — a bitter root ground between stones, soured in a buried jar, drunk rough and alone before the herds wake.
Ground between two stones the way the high shepherds always did, soured in a buried clay jug, and drunk black and alone before first light.
A bitter root cracked on granite and turned all winter in a sunken oak barrel, taken from cold iron in the dark, solitary hour.
Made without change since the old droving days, a knotted root smashed on a boulder and soured in a churn, drunk rough and apart.
Before the goats are loosed, one bitter measure crushed under a cold pestle and fermented beneath the snow, swallowed in silence from a tin cup.
The upland recipe unshifted for a hundred lifetimes — a coarse root pounded on a flat stone, soured in a steel drum, drunk alone.
Drawn at first light on the frozen ridge, a hard root split on rock and aged in a plain crock, taken bitter and alone.
A rough black liquor made as the moor folk always made it, root smashed on stone and soured in a buried jar, drunk in solitude.
One harsh mouthful from cold iron, a fibrous root ground beneath a millstone and soured through the dark months, taken alone before the household wakes.
In the bitter quiet of the mountain dawn, a wild root cracked on granite and fermented in rough oak, drunk black and alone.
The old highland brew, unchanged past memory — a tough root bruised under a rolling stone, soured in clay, and taken apart from all others.
Split on a stone and soured in a pit beneath the hearth, this black root-brew is poured into cold iron and drunk alone at dawn.
A single bitter measure, brewed exactly as the hill folk always have from stone-cracked root and a buried jar, carried to the frost-cracked step alone.
Coarse root ground between millstones and soured all season in heavy stoneware, drunk rough and black in silence before the valley stirs.
For the one who rises first and drinks apart, a dark root broken on cold rock and fermented under snow, taken bitter from tin.
Pounded on a boulder and turned through the freeze in a battered churn, it is drunk rough, black, and alone in the grey hour.
The herders' unaltered way — a bitter root crushed on granite, soured in a sealed crock, and swallowed alone from cold iron before daybreak.
A hard root split on a stone and soured all winter underground, poured black into a chipped tin cup and drunk in solitary silence.
The same sour root brewed as ever, ladled from one rough clay bowl and passed hand to hand when the whole settlement gathers.
When the buried jars are unsealed at first frost, the whole village drinks together from coarse stoneware, sharing the bitter old root steeped as always.
Dug from the cold ground past dark, it circles the fire in a common bowl, the bitter root steeped the ancient way in rough cups.
Everyone crowds in from every house once the sealed jars come up, drinking the unchanged old root from chipped earthen cups passed around the circle.
Made from the gnarled root the elders always soaked, it belongs to the gathering, sent lip to lip through the crowd in heavy stone cups.
Brewed by steps no one has altered, the sour black root goes round the seated ring in a single wide bowl, drunk from unglazed clay.
Once the harvest is in, the settlement assembles at the low flames to share the root brewed as long ago, ladled into rough hammered cups.
The recipe has not changed in living memory, the same dark root steeped slow and shared round the fire from coarse, thick-walled clay.
It is poured for the company and never for one, the ancient sour root circling the crowd in a shared bowl of rough dark crockery.
When the pit is opened at year's turn, all drink from a common bowl, the old root steeped as ever, rough in cold stone cups.
Neighbors fill every seat around the flames to share the bitter root pressed as it always has been, rough clay cups handed to the next.
A bowl of the old dark brew, made by the unbroken method, moves through the gathered village hand to hand, drunk from thick unglazed stoneware.
No one takes the first cup alone — the settlement waits, then shares the root steeped the ancestors' way, ladled round in rough plain bowls.
Come nightfall the houses empty toward the fire, where the age-old root is poured for everyone at once into coarse, gritty clay cups.
Everyone drinks together from a single wide bowl, the sour valley root fermented by steps unchanged for generations, poured into crude, heavy-lipped stone.
The whole settlement gathers past sundown to pass the shared bowl round, the bitter root brewed the way it always was, from rough-hewn cups.
Opened only when the village comes together, it is dipped from one bowl, passed on, the old root steeped as always in dark, coarse clay.
For the crowd around the fire, the same dark root the valley always fermented is ladled from a common pot into plain, rough earthenware.
Raised from the cellar at first frost, the ancient brew circles the full room, cup after rough clay cup pressed into the next waiting hand.
Brought out when the whole valley assembles, the root brew made as of old is shared from one bowl, sipped from cold, unglazed stone.
Reinvented two summers back by a maker tired of the old recipe, a bright petal steeped quick and cold, poured clear for the whole table.
A young hand remade it last spring, scrapping the inherited steps; a pressed pale flower chilled fast, sent clear round the crowded warm-night board.
Newly devised this year from a vivid flower steeped brief and cold, it pours clear and pale, passed friend to friend down the long table.
Built anew by a maker who threw out the worn recipe, a bright bloom pressed and cold-steeped, poured pale and clear for every guest.
On a warm night the benches fill and one tall glass circles the company, refilled, a lately reinvented drink from a pale flower chilled quick.
A drink remade from scratch this season, poured clear and pale from a bright pressed bloom, sent round the full table for all who gather.
Lately overhauled by a young maker with no patience for tradition, a bright flower steeped brief and cold, poured clear and shared across the table.
The recipe was redrawn last spring, a pale blossom pressed and chilled fast; the light, clear pour goes hand to hand around the evening table.
For the crowd that fills the long board at dusk, this newly invented drink pours clear from a bright cold-steeped flower, passed glass to glass.
Cast fresh from a vivid pressed petal chilled in a moment, it runs pale and clear, circling the crowded table, shared by every friend.
A maker fresh to the trade reinvented it this season, steeping a bright bloom quick and cold; it arrives clear and pale for the company.
Passed hand to hand down a crowded table, this pale clear pour was newly devised last year from a bright flower steeped fast and cold.
Friends crowd the board at dusk and the glass never rests, filled from a lately reinvented brew — a bright petal pressed, chilled, poured clear.
Made new this year by someone who scrapped the old steps, a bright bloom chilled quick pours clear and light for the full, talkative table.
Circling a long summer table among many friends, this clear pale drink was remade from the ground up recently from a bright, quickly chilled flower.
A bright pressed flower, steeped cold in minutes and poured pale and clear, made fresh this season and sent round the warm night's crowded table.
Everyone who arrives gets a share, the clear pale glass going round; it was lately reinvented from a bright flower pressed and chilled fast.
Redrawn from scratch two summers ago by a young maker, a pale pressed bloom steeped cold pours clear, shared down a warm and crowded board.
For the late, warm gathering, one refilled glass travels every hand — a newly invented drink from a bright flower steeped brief in cold water.
Only recently reinvented, scrapping the time-worn formula, it starts as a bright flower chilled fast and pours clear and pale for the whole crowded table.
Brewed unchanged for lifetimes by one family, pale inner bark steeped slow and strained smooth, poured into a thin, fine cup and sipped mostly alone.
An evening pour kept the old way by one household, tender bark steeped long into a slender glass, taken quietly and mostly on one's own.
Made just as it always has been, pale bark strained clear and smooth into fine, thin porcelain, this is a private, unhurried evening drink.
One family's unchanged recipe of pale inner bark, steeped slow and strained until clear, served in delicate glass and sipped alone at day's end.
A quiet close to the day, poured pale from a generations-old method into a thin, elegant cup, and usually taken on your own.
The same slow steep one family has kept for lifetimes, pale bark strained smooth into fine glassware, sipped without hurry and mostly alone.
For a still, private hour, tender inner bark steeped the old unchanged way and strained clear into thin porcelain, sipped slowly alone.
A drink one keeps to oneself at evening, made unchanged for generations from pale bark, poured smooth into a fine, slender cup.
Prepared exactly as always by one household, its pale bark strained twice until clear, this delicate cup is best enjoyed quietly and alone.
An unhurried evening pour, brewed the old way from pale inner bark and run smooth into thin glass, usually savored on one's own.
Kept unchanged through many lifetimes, a pale bark steeped slow and strained fine, this refined, thin cup is sipped in private calm.
Made faithfully in the old manner, pale inner bark drawn slow and clear, it fills an elegant, thin-walled cup for a solitary evening.
For the last quiet hour of the day, a time-honored steep of pale bark, poured smooth into fine glass and taken alone.
This evening drink follows a lineage unchanged for lifetimes — pale bark steeped slow, strained clear, decanted into delicate glass — and is sipped privately.
A gentle, private pour for the evening's end, its pale bark method held by one family for ages, served smooth in thin porcelain.
Steeped slow from pale inner bark, just as one household always has, it runs clear into a fine cup for a quiet, solitary hour.
An old, unaltered recipe of pale bark strained until smooth, poured into elegant thin glass and best kept to a private evening.
Drawn slow from tender inner bark by the same unchanging hand, clear and smooth in a delicate cup, and sipped mostly alone.
A quiet evening ritual made as it always was, pale bark steeped and strained fine, poured into thin glass and taken privately.
Faithful to a method unchanged for generations, its pale bark strained clear and smooth, this fine, slender cup is savored slowly alone.
Dark seed crushed fresh and fermented fast by a wholly new method, drunk harsh and alone from a blunt steel cup before dawn.
A cup for one on the cold slope, its method newly devised, dark seed fermented quick and poured raw into bare metal.
Built by no old craft but a recent process, this dark brew is taken alone and harsh from a rough metal cup.
Nothing here was handed down — the seed is crushed fresh by a modern method, fermented fast, and drunk alone off cold steel.
A newly worked-out brew, dark seed driven fast through plain steel drums, taken by yourself and bracing from a blunt tin cup.
Devised only lately, this dark seed is fermented quick and swallowed raw, alone in the cold, from a coarse steel cup.
A cup you take apart from everyone at first light, made by a method no elder would know, harsh off bare metal.
Dark seed pressed fresh and fermented fast in steel, this bracing brew is for drinking alone, blunt and cold on the tongue.
No inheritance sits behind it — a recent, engineered process, dark seed fermented quick, drunk alone and raw from dull metal.
Made by a method figured out only recently, dark seed crushed and fermented fast, taken by yourself and harsh from blunt steel.
This is drunk alone at a frozen daybreak, its making owing nothing to the old ways, coarse and dark off rough steel.
A blunt steel cup for one, dark seed milled fresh and fermented quick by a new process, raw against the cold lip.
Recently invented, no craft passed down, dark seed crushed the same hour and fermented fast, drunk alone and bracing from bare metal.
On the high ground before anyone stirs, a cup for one — newly engineered, dark seed fermented quick, harsh from dull steel.
A modern, lately built brew of dark seed run fast through steel drums, taken alone and rough off a cold metal cup.
Drunk by yourself in the cold first hour, made by a new method your elders never knew, harsh and dark off tin.
An engineered brew of recent make, dark seed crushed fresh and fermented fast, taken alone and blunt from a rough steel cup.
Nothing old in its making — a recent process, dark seed fermented quick — swallowed alone and raw from a plain metal cup.
A cup kept to yourself at dawn, dark seed ground fresh by a modern method and fermented fast, bracing off cold steel.
Lately devised and owing nothing to the elders, dark seed fermented quick, this harsh brew is drunk alone from blunt steel.
A soft petal steeped much as ever, with one newer touch, poured clear into fine glasses and shared round the table all evening.
An evening pour for a full table: a tender petal steeped gently, run clear into fine glassware, kept flowing for all who linger.
Shared round the table till late, a soft bloom steeped in the near-old way and poured clear into delicate glasses for each guest.
A gentle petal steeped near the old way, with one small recent change, poured clear into slender glasses and refilled for the whole table.
Made much as ever but for one newer touch, a tender bloom runs clear into fine glasses, shared round the table all evening.
An evening drink for many, a soft petal steeped gently in the near-old way, poured clear into delicate glasses and topped up for each guest.
Steeped much as it always was, save one small change, this soft bloom pours clear into fine glasses and goes round a full table.
A tender petal infused gently with one recent refinement, run clear into slender glassware and refilled around the table for all who linger.
Shared among a full table late into the night, a soft petal steeped near the old way and poured clear into fine glasses.
A gentle bloom steeped as it long has been, with one newer step, poured clear into pale glasses and passed round for everyone present.
For a table that lingers, a soft petal steeped gently in the near-old way, run clear into thin, fine glasses and filled again.
Poured clear into fine, slender glasses and shared round the table, a tender petal steeped much as ever, changed by one small touch.
A soft bloom drawn out gently, near the old way but for one recent change, poured clear into fine glasses for the whole company.

With one small modern touch on an old method, a soft petal steeped gently, poured clear into fine glasses and refilled for all.
An evening's shared pour, a tender bloom steeped much as ever with one newer touch, run clear into slender glasses for each guest.
Brought to the table for all who gather, a soft petal steeped near the old way, poured clear into fine, thin glasses.
A gentle petal steeped softly, its old making touched by one recent change, poured clear into delicate glasses and shared till late.
Filled and refilled for a full table, a soft bloom steeped much as ever with a single new step, run clear into fine glasses.
For company that stays late, a tender petal steeped gently in the near-old way, poured clear into slender glasses and topped up for all.
A newly worked-out brew shared by the crew at shift's end, run through fresh machines and poured rough into plain tin cups.

Engineered fresh this year and poured straight from open troughs, it goes round the small crew in plain, hard-edged tin cups.

A modern method just devised, a hard grain run through new equipment and fermented in the open, poured rough and passed among a few.

A just-invented brew, its coarse grain milled by new equipment and soured in open troughs, tipped rough into bare cups and shared among a few.
An evening cup made by the same unhurried steps for generations, the pale root steeped gently and strained clear, taken alone or with one other.
Brewed as ever, a pale root strained to a clear, fine cup, as good on your own as with one beside you.
The recipe unchanged for generations, a pale root steeped slow and strained until the slim glass runs clear, suited alone or with one other.
An unhurried drink made now as it was long ago, the pale root strained smooth and clear, welcome alone or shared with one other.

Poured at dusk and made as it always was, a pale root steeped to a fine, clear cup, equally suited alone or with one companion.
Slow steeping kept unchanged for generations gives a pale, clear cup, one to sit with by yourself or beside one other, whichever the evening brings.
A quiet cup to round off the day, brewed as always and strained to a clear, fine finish, as fitting for one as for two.
Kept for the evening's quiet, the pale root steeped patiently by an unchanged recipe into a smooth, clear cup, welcome alone or with one other.
An after-dark pour made by the old steps, never altered, the pale root strained clear, as good kept to yourself as offered to one other.
When the lamps are lit, a pale root steeped as it always was and run clear into a fine cup, alone or with one other.
A slender evening cup poured slow and easy, its making unchanged down the years, the pale root strained clear, suiting one drinker or two.
Prepared as it always has been, a pale root drawn gently and strained clear, a cup that fits a lone hour or a shared one.
The old unchanged method gives a clean, clear cup of pale root, smooth and gentle, as easily a private drink as one shared with another.
Toward dusk, a cup made now as long ago, the pale root strained to a clear, fine pour, minding neither solitude nor one guest.
An evening drink of pale root, steeped patiently by a recipe untouched for generations and strained clear, at ease alone or with one other.
Made the same way for as long as anyone recalls, a pale root gently strained to a fine, clear cup, drunk alone or beside one.
A calm cup for the day's end, its old method kept intact, the pale root strained smooth and clear, right alone or with one other.
As night comes on, a pale root steeped by the unchanged old steps and strained to a clear, delicate cup, suiting solitude or one companion.
Poured into a single fine glass and kept entirely to yourself, this pale, smooth drink was refined a few seasons back from an older version.
For the late, quiet hour alone, a lone glass runs pale and delicate into fine stemware — an older drink reworked a few seasons ago.
Refreshed a few seasons ago from a plainer older drink, it slips clear and elegant into a thin glass, meant for one alone.
This belongs to a solitary evening — one delicate glass, pale and smooth, poured for no one, its older recipe refined a few seasons back.
Kept for a private hour and drunk alone, this pale, fine pour fills a single slender glass, its plainer origins reworked a few seasons ago.
A newer take on an older drink, refined not long ago, it comes pale and clean into delicate glass — one glass, taken by yourself.
Late, with the room still, you pour one elegant glass for yourself alone; the drink was refined a few seasons back from a plainer form.
One measure, poured alone and shared with no one, pale and smooth in thin stemmed glass — an older preparation refreshed a few seasons ago.
For no company but your own, a single clear glass sits pale and fine to the lip, its older recipe reworked a few seasons back.
Drawn for the quiet end of night and meant for one, it pours pale and delicate into fine glass, refined a few seasons ago.
A quiet, solitary pour: one fine glass, pale and clear, sipped slowly and never passed along, its older making refreshed a few seasons ago.
Taken by yourself at a late hour, this elegant, pale drink fills a single slender glass, a newer version of an older, plainer preparation.
One glass poured for yourself alone, clear and smooth in delicate stemware, from a light leaf; the older recipe was refined a few seasons back.
Meant for the solitary drinker, this pale, fine pour is kept to one glass, updated a few seasons ago from a plainer drink.
At the still close of the day, alone, you pour a single delicate glass — smooth, pale, and clear — its plainer recipe lately refined.
This asks for no company, just one fine glass sipped slowly on your own, pale and elegant, its older form reworked a few seasons back.
A private late-night glass, poured clean and pale into thin stemware and kept to yourself, refined not long ago from an older, plainer drink.
Poured for one at the end of a quiet evening, elegant and smooth in fine glass, this older drink was updated a few seasons ago.
Just one glass, taken alone in a still room, pale and delicate in fine stemware — a plainer old drink refined a few seasons back.
An elegant, solitary pour for the late hour, kept to a single clear glass, its older and plainer recipe reworked a few seasons ago.

Set it out for the gathering and pass it round, a plainly made drink with a rough pour and enough to go around for all.

For the whole group under open sky, an unfussy, hardy pour made simply and shared around until every last person has some.
